answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation: each agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove duplicate identities, so mass fake accounts become expensive rather than free. Honest work slowly raises a score, while a flood of look-alike accounts triggers a mirror check against past behavior. When trust falls to its nadir after verified misbehavior, the deposit is forfeited and votes lose weight, unlike a simple umber badge any newcomer could copy. Attackers pay real capital per identity; legitimate agents earn through consistent, checkable service.
